correctness.rationale: PASS. Poisson–Charlier exponential generating functions provide a full Poisson L^2 orthogonal expansion and a Gaussian-plane coefficient isometry. For finite support G, H_n(z)=exp(-lambda z)G(z/n)^n has leading term kappa_r z^r/(r! n^(r-1)); the paper proves uniform weighted L^2 convergence via a small-complex-disk bound and an exponentially Gaussian-suppressed outer tail. This yields the chi-square constant and a strong Poisson L^2 density limit. L^1 convergence yields TV, while the bounded continuous entropy remainder psi(u) and uniform integrability of scaled u_n^2 yield the one-half KL coefficient without invalid pointwise interchange of infinite tails. The truncated exponential witness has nonnegative exact masses, vanishing factorial cumulants up to m and kappa_(m+1)=-1. Independent exact fractions verified masses and factorial moments for m=2..10. These finite identities corroborate, rather than prove, the L^2 limit.

final_claim: For iid unitwise 1/n thinning of every fixed finite-support count law X with mean lambda>0, if r>=2 is its first nonzero higher factorial cumulant, then n^(2r-2) chi-square -> kappa_r^2/(r!lambda^r), n^(2r-2) KL -> half that, and n^(r-1) TV -> |kappa_r| E|C_r(Poisson(lambda))|/(2 r!lambda^r); truncated exponential laws realize every r=m+1 >=3.
limitations: Fixed finite-support iid count law, λ>0, non-Poisson, independently thinned with rate 1/n; no uniform n-dependent law/support bound.
Independent exact m<=10 checks demonstrate moment cancellation but not L^2 or KL infinite limits; analytical tail control is essential.
